frontier.hypothesis: Every score banked in this ledger must be re-audited detector-complete before any of it is spent: the cheat-stripper silently removes some spellings (making a 12 an artifact of the strip, not a codegen fact) and misses others (making a 0 an artifact of a hole).
frontier.mechanism: engine/volatile_cheats.py strips find_unused_local_arrays matches (array declarators, 2 <= n <= 64, zero references), find_void_discard_unused_locals matches, and find_orphaned_local_decls matches; anything outside those regexes compiles as written. Only a real unstripped build (`make build/src/text1b.o` + objdump) is codegen evidence.
frontier.next_probe: For each form in memory/grind/func_80049A2C/rejected/, record BOTH the real frame from an unstripped build AND the sandbox score, and mark which rows are strip artifacts. tmp/grind/func_80049A2C/s6/matrix.md already does this for 10 rows and is the template; the pre-s6 rows (scalar-dummy-no-frame.c, struct-dummy-h8-same-frame-same-defect.c, the s2 phantom-injection variants) have never been measured this way.

frontier.hypothesis: Frame 0x30 is reachable with vars = 0 by raising current_function_outgoing_args_size from 16 to 24 (0 + 24 + 20 -> ALIGN8 -> 48), which needs no local at all and therefore no dead declaration.
frontier.mechanism: MIPS compute_frame_size takes args_size from the widest call in the function, floored at REG_PARM_STACK_SPACE = 16. All three calls here take <= 1 argument. Some back-end-emitted library calls, alloca, and __builtin_apply bump outgoing_args_size by paths other than an explicit fifth argument.
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate the constructs that bump outgoing_args_size WITHOUT emitting an argument store (64-bit shift/divide/soft-float helpers, alloca, __builtin_apply) and test whether any is reachable from a semantic rewrite of this body that keeps build_insns at 126. Prior expectation is negative (a fifth integer argument stores at 0x10($sp), which target lacks), but this is the last decomposition of the frame equation never measured, and s6 proved the equation had been mis-derived once already.

frontier.hypothesis: The three cheat-stripper spelling holes are an operator-side defect that makes any function's sandbox 0 suspect when it depends on a dead local.
frontier.mechanism: (1) _ORPHAN_DECL_RE's `;[ \t]*$` anchor is defeated by a trailing comment on the declaration line; (2) neither find_unused_local_arrays nor find_orphaned_local_decls has a struct/union arm, so a zero-reference struct-typed local is never stripped; (3) _VOID_DISCARD_NO_ADDR_RE covers `(void) name;` but not `(void) name[0];`.
frontier.next_probe: Operator item, not a grind probe - engine/ is outside the grind-session surface. Filed in the 2026-08-19 correction entry at the tail of docs/grind/decisions.md. Until it is closed, treat any dead-local-dependent 0 elsewhere in the queue as unverified.
